import pandas as pd

def clean(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # 1. Drop exact duplicate rows
    df = df.drop_duplicates().copy()

    # 2. Standardize text columns (strip spaces, fix known variants, lower‑case where appropriate)
    # species
    species_map = {
        "Adeile": "Adelie",
        "adelie": "Adelie",
        "Adelie": "Adelie",
        "Gentoo": "Gentoo",
        "Chinstrap": "Chinstrap"
    }
    df["species"] = df["species"].str.strip().map(species_map).fillna(df["species"].str.strip())

    # island – just strip leading/trailing spaces
    df["island"] = df["island"].str.strip()

    # sex – normalize case, treat "FEMALE" as "female"
    df["sex"] = df["sex"].str.strip().str.lower()
    df["sex"] = df["sex"].replace({"female": "female", "male": "male"})

    # 3. Convert numeric‑as‑text columns to proper numeric dtype
    for col in ["flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g"]:
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

    # 4. Enforce allowed ranges for body_mass_g (2500‑6500 g). Values outside become NaN.
    df.loc[~df["body_mass_g"].between(2500, 6500), "body_mass_g"] = pd.NA

    return df

def answer(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    clean_df = clean(df)
    # Compute average body mass per species, ignoring missing values
    result_series = clean_df.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"].mean()
    # Convert to plain Python types (float) and drop any species that ended up with NaN mean
    result = {species: float(avg) for species, avg in result_series.items() if pd.notna(avg)}
    return result
